summary:
Gombe State criminalises same-sex conduct under its own Shari'a Penal Code Law 2001, signed into law on 23 November 2001, which operates alongside Nigeria's federal criminal law. Human Rights Watch's 2004 report on Shari'a implementation lists Gombe among the twelve northern states that had adopted Shari'a into criminal legislation by 2002, with Shari'a courts holding criminal jurisdiction over Muslims beyond the federal code.

The enacted penalties are severe and gendered. Gombe, Jigawa, Kano and Zamfara share a sodomy offence that punishes unmarried men with caning of 100 lashes plus one year's imprisonment and married men with stoning to death (rajm); the lesbianism offence carries up to 50 lashes plus imprisonment of up to six months. Gombe defines gross indecency in its own formulation as "any sexual offence against the normal or usual standards of behaviour", and the enacted statutory text criminalises same-sex conduct by men and women beyond the federal code.

The UK Home Office country-of-origin information note on sexual orientation and gender identity in Nigeria (June 2025) states that Islamic law applies to Muslims in the twelve northern states, which include Gombe, and criminalises same-sex sexual acts both between men and between women. The maximum penalty for "sodomy" for men is death in all twelve states, and penalties for "lesbianism" range from death to flogging and imprisonment. The note carries a dedicated section on enforcement of Shari'a provisions and on the attitude of the hisbah, the morality police.

Enforcement in Gombe is documented at scale on one occasion. In October 2023 the Gombe State Command of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps raided a birthday gathering at Duwa Plaza along the Bauchi-Gombe Expressway that was preparing a same-sex wedding, arresting 76 people. State PRO Buhari Sa'ad told reporters that 59 males were detained, 21 of whom wilfully confessed to being homosexuals, and that 17 females were present at the scene; the detainees would be charged to court to answer for their crime, which he described as a social vice and a crime in Gombe State. Gombe NSCDC Commandant Mohammed Muazu confirmed the arrests to The Guardian of 23 October 2023, whose report by James Agberebi states that the remaining males and the 17 females were invited guests and onlookers, and records officers' concern over the ages of the participants. The October 2023 raid is the most recent documented enforcement action in this record; no later instance is documented.
tangentialFactors:
The Gombe raid belongs to a documented national pattern of security operations against private gatherings and hotels: more than 100 people were arrested at a hotel party in Asaba, Delta State in June 2018, 57 young men at a hotel in Egbeda, Lagos in August 2018, and 67 people in Warri, Delta State in August 2023. The Gombe figure of 76 arrests is a raw count; such counts track the size of the event and the population of the jurisdiction, and no per-capita comparison between these states is available in the sources.

Gombe's sodomy and lesbianism offences are shared verbatim with Jigawa, Kano and Zamfara, so the penalty structure a visitor faces in Gombe is the standard northern Shari'a formulation rather than a local variation. The distinguishing regional feature is enforcement machinery: the UK Home Office note of June 2025 treats the twelve northern states as a single block for Shari'a penalties and gives enforcement of Shari'a provisions and the attitude of the hisbah their own section, which is not a feature of the secular southern enforcement picture.

Charging practice in Gombe rests on a broad local offence. The state command's stated basis for charging the October 2023 attendees was "social vice", a category that does not require proof of a completed sexual act, and 21 of the 59 detained males were reported as having wilfully confessed.
localsOnly:
Muslim residents of Gombe fall under Shari'a courts holding criminal jurisdiction beyond the federal code, a status Human Rights Watch recorded as established by 2002. The 2001 Penal Code applies to them directly, with the stoning penalty for married men and 100 lashes plus a year's imprisonment for unmarried men set out in the enacted text.

The hisbah, Gombe's morality police, operates under the Shari'a enforcement layer that the UK Home Office note of June 2025 examines for the twelve northern states, and its conduct is a resident-facing condition of daily life rather than an airport or border issue.

Residents are exposed to the gross indecency definition in Gombe's own wording, "any sexual offence against the normal or usual standards of behaviour", which is drafted around perceived standards rather than around a specified act. The 76 people arrested in October 2023 were state residents and guests, and the state command's spokesperson stated they would be charged in Gombe State courts.
outOfScopeNotes:
The outcome of the October 2023 charges is unresolved in this record. No source states whether the 76 detainees were convicted, acquitted or released, and no later proceeding is documented.

No region-specific documentation was identified for violence against transgender people in Gombe, for hate-crime or anti-discrimination provisions at state level, or for legal gender recognition. Whether Gombe has any such instrument is not sourced either way.

The hisbah material in the UK Home Office note of June 2025 covers the twelve northern states as a group; specific hisbah arrests or interventions in Gombe are not sourced. Whether the hisbah or the state police have acted against individuals under the 2001 law outside the October 2023 raid is unresolved.

Whether the Shari'a Penal Code Law 2001 has been amended since it was signed on 23 November 2001 is not sourced. The most recent documented enforcement in Gombe is October 2023, and the absence of later reports in this record does not establish that enforcement has stopped.
